Opaque handle for an Opus decoder state. Full definition is hidden; create with opus_decoder_create() or allocate opus_decoder_get_size() bytes and call opus_decoder_init(). Not thread-safe for concurrent access.
Opaque handle for the Opus DRED (decoder-side redundancy) decoder state used to parse and process DRED data accompanying Opus packets.
Opaque handle for Opus DRED state representing a decoded/parsed DRED packet payload. Allocated with opus_dred_alloc() and freed with opus_dred_free().

functions.name: opus_strerror
functions.signature: const char *opus_strerror(int error)
functions.description: Converts a libopus error code to a human-readable, null-terminated string. Use this to log or display textual descriptions of return codes from Opus APIs. The returned pointer refers to a constant string owned by the library (inferred: do not modify or free).
requirements: Argument error should be an error code returned by libopus functions (e.g., OPUS_OK, OPUS_BAD_ARG, etc.).
Returned string is read-only and must not be freed (inferred from return type and typical API behavior).

functions.name: opus_get_version_string
functions.signature: const char *opus_get_version_string(void)
functions.description: Returns the libopus version string describing the build. Applications may look for the substring "-fixed" to detect fixed-point builds at runtime. The returned pointer refers to a constant, null-terminated string owned by the library (inferred: do not modify or free).
requirements: No arguments required.
Returned string is read-only and must not be freed (inferred from return type and typical API behavior).

functions.name: opus_encoder_get_size
functions.signature: int opus_encoder_get_size(int channels);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusEncoder state for a given channel count. Use before allocating memory for manual initialization.
requirements: channels must be 1 or 2
The returned size may overestimate for OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_SILK and OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_CELT (note for sizing copies)

functions.name: opus_encoder_create
functions.signature: OpusEncoder *opus_encoder_create(opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int application, int *error);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an Opus encoder state for the specified sample rate, channel count, and application/mode.
requirements: channels must be 1 or 2
application must be one of OPUS_APPLICATION_VOIP, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, or OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY
error must be a valid pointer if error reporting is desired; on success set to OPUS_OK, otherwise an opus_errorcodes value
A single encoder state must not be used concurrently for more than one stream or re-initialized for each frame

functions.name: opus_encoder_init
functions.signature: int opus_encoder_init(OpusEncoder *st, opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int application);
functions.description: Initializes a pre-allocated OpusEncoder at the given sample rate, channels, and application. Use with custom allocation or to reset configuration.
requirements: st must point to memory of at least opus_encoder_get_size(channels) bytes
channels must be 1 or 2
application must be OPUS_APPLICATION_VOIP, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, or OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY
To reset an already initialized state at runtime, use OPUS_RESET_STATE via opus_encoder_ctl() rather than calling this again

functions.name: opus_encode
functions.signature: opus_int32 opus_encode(OpusEncoder *st, const opus_int16 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes);
functions.description: Encodes a single Opus frame from 16-bit integer PCM into a compressed packet.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved input of length frame_size*channels samples (opus_int16)
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder’s sampling rate (e.g., at 48 kHz: 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920, 2880)
Providing less than 10 ms (e.g., <480 at 48 kHz) prevents use of LPC or hybrid modes
data must have at least max_data_bytes capacity
max_data_bytes is an upper bound on output size; do not use it for bitrate control (use OPUS_SET_BITRATE)
Returns number of bytes written on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_encode24
functions.signature: opus_int32 opus_encode24(OpusEncoder *st, const opus_int32 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes);
functions.description: Encodes a single Opus frame from 24-bit-depth (packed in 32-bit int) PCM into a compressed packet.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved input of length frame_size*channels samples (opus_int32 representing or slightly exceeding 24-bit)
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder’s sampling rate (see opus_encode for examples)
Providing less than 10 ms prevents LPC/hybrid modes
data must have at least max_data_bytes capacity
Returns number of bytes written on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_encode_float
functions.signature: opus_int32 opus_encode_float(OpusEncoder *st, const float *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes);
functions.description: Encodes a single Opus frame from 32-bit float PCM into a compressed packet. Normalized input range is +/-1.0.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved float samples of length frame_size*channels
Samples outside +/-1.0 are allowed but will be clipped by integer decoders; only use if far end supports extended dynamic range
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder’s sampling rate; <10 ms duration prevents LPC/hybrid modes
data must have at least max_data_bytes capacity
Returns number of bytes written on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_encoder_destroy
functions.signature: void opus_encoder_destroy(OpusEncoder *st);
functions.description: Frees an OpusEncoder allocated by opus_encoder_create(). No action needed for encoders initialized via opus_encoder_init() aside from freeing user memory.
requirements: st must be a pointer returned by opus_encoder_create() or NULL (freeing a NULL is a no-op in many implementations, behavior unspecified here)

functions.name: opus_encoder_ctl
functions.signature: int opus_encoder_ctl(OpusEncoder *st, int request, ...);
functions.description: Applies a control (CTL) request to an Opus encoder to set or query parameters. Requests/args are provided via convenience macros from opus_genericctls/opus_encoderctls.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusEncoder
request must be one of the documented CTL macros; remaining varargs must match the request’s expected types
Most parameters can be set or changed at any time during a stream

functions.name: opus_decoder_get_size
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_get_size(int channels);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusDecoder state for a given channel count.
requirements: channels must be 1 or 2

functions.name: opus_decoder_create
functions.signature: OpusDecoder *opus_decoder_create(opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int *error);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an Opus decoder state for the specified output sample rate and channel count.
requirements: channels must be 1 or 2
error must be a valid pointer if error reporting is desired; set to OPUS_OK on success, otherwise an opus_errorcodes value
Packets must be fed sequentially in correct order to decode properly; loss can be indicated with data=NULL and len=0 to invoke PLC
A single decoder state may only be accessed from a single thread at a time (caller must provide locking if needed)

functions.name: opus_decoder_init
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_init(OpusDecoder *st, opus_int32 Fs, int channels);
functions.description: Initializes a pre-allocated OpusDecoder to decode at the specified sample rate and channels.
requirements: st must point to memory of at least opus_decoder_get_size(channels) bytes
channels must be 1 or 2
To reset an initialized state use OPUS_RESET_STATE via opus_decoder_ctl()

functions.name: opus_decode
functions.signature: int opus_decode(OpusDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int16 *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec);
functions.description: Decodes an Opus packet into 16-bit PCM. Supports packet loss concealment (PLC) with data=NULL and len=0, and optional in-band FEC when available.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
data points to compressed payload; use NULL to indicate packet loss
len is number of bytes in payload
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (opus_int16)
frame_size is available space per channel; if less than max packet duration (120 ms; 5760 at 48 kHz), some packets cannot be decoded
For PLC (data==NULL) or FEC (decode_fec=1), frame_size must exactly match the missing audio duration and must be a multiple of 2.5 ms
decode_fec must be 0 or 1
Returns samples per channel on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_decode24
functions.signature: int opus_decode24(OpusDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int32 *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec);
functions.description: Decodes an Opus packet into 24-bit-depth (packed in 32-bit int) PCM. Supports PLC and optional FEC when available.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
data points to compressed payload; NULL to indicate loss
len is number of bytes in payload
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (opus_int32)
frame_size rules identical to opus_decode (must be adequate; for PLC/FEC exact missing duration and multiple of 2.5 ms)
decode_fec must be 0 or 1
Returns number of decoded samples on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_decode_float
functions.signature: int opus_decode_float(OpusDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, float *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec);
functions.description: Decodes an Opus packet into 32-bit float PCM. Supports PLC and optional FEC when available.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
data points to compressed payload; NULL to indicate loss
len is number of bytes in payload
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (float)
frame_size rules identical to opus_decode (adequate buffer; PLC/FEC exact missing duration and multiple of 2.5 ms)
decode_fec must be 0 or 1
Returns samples per channel on success; negative values are opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_decoder_ctl
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_ctl(OpusDecoder *st, int request, ...);
functions.description: Applies a control (CTL) request to an Opus decoder to set or query parameters. Requests/args via opus_genericctls/opus_decoderctls macros.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
request must be a documented CTL; varargs must match the request’s expected types
A single decoder state may only be accessed from one thread at a time; caller synchronization required if shared

functions.name: opus_decoder_destroy
functions.signature: void opus_decoder_destroy(OpusDecoder *st);
functions.description: Frees an OpusDecoder allocated by opus_decoder_create(). Not needed for decoders initialized with opus_decoder_init() aside from user memory free.
requirements: st should be a pointer returned by opus_decoder_create()

functions.name: opus_dred_decoder_get_size
functions.signature: int opus_dred_decoder_get_size(void);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusDREDDecoder state.

functions.name: opus_dred_decoder_create
functions.signature: OpusDREDDecoder *opus_dred_decoder_create(int *error);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an Opus DRED decoder state.
requirements: error should be a valid pointer if error reporting is desired; set to OPUS_OK on success or an opus_errorcodes value

functions.name: opus_dred_decoder_init
functions.signature: int opus_dred_decoder_init(OpusDREDDecoder *dec);
functions.description: Initializes a pre-allocated OpusDREDDecoder state.
requirements: dec must point to memory of at least opus_dred_decoder_get_size() bytes

functions.name: opus_dred_decoder_destroy
functions.signature: void opus_dred_decoder_destroy(OpusDREDDecoder *dec);
functions.description: Frees an OpusDREDDecoder allocated by opus_dred_decoder_create().
requirements: dec should be a pointer returned by opus_dred_decoder_create()

functions.name: opus_dred_decoder_ctl
functions.signature: int opus_dred_decoder_ctl(OpusDREDDecoder *dred_dec, int request, ...);
functions.description: Applies a CTL request to an Opus DRED decoder to set/query parameters. Requests/args via generic/decoder CTL macros.
requirements: dred_dec must be a valid, initialized OpusDREDDecoder
request must be a documented CTL macro; varargs must match expected types

functions.name: opus_dred_get_size
functions.signature: int opus_dred_get_size(void);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusDRED state (per-packet DRED data).

functions.name: opus_dred_alloc
functions.signature: OpusDRED *opus_dred_alloc(int *error);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new OpusDRED state (to hold DRED packet data).
requirements: error should be a valid pointer if error reporting is desired; set to OPUS_OK on success or an opus_errorcodes value

functions.name: opus_dred_free
functions.signature: void opus_dred_free(OpusDRED *dec);
functions.description: Frees an OpusDRED state previously allocated by opus_dred_alloc().
requirements: dec should be a pointer returned by opus_dred_alloc()

functions.name: opus_dred_parse
functions.signature: int opus_dred_parse(OpusDREDDecoder *dred_dec, OpusDRED *dred, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int32 max_dred_samples, opus_int32 sampling_rate, int *dred_end, int defer_processing);
functions.description: Parses and optionally partially decodes a DRED payload from an Opus packet. May defer CPU-intensive processing until opus_dred_process() if requested.
requirements: dred_dec must be a valid, initialized OpusDREDDecoder
dred must be a valid OpusDRED state to receive parsed data
data points to input payload; len is its size in bytes
max_dred_samples is the maximum number of DRED samples that may be needed (if available)
sampling_rate is used to interpret max_dred_samples and need not match the decoder’s actual rate
dred_end must be a valid pointer to receive the count of trailing non-encoded (silence) samples between the DRED timestamp and last DRED sample
defer_processing must be 0 or 1; if 1, finish with opus_dred_process()
Returns positive offset of first decoded DRED samples, 0 if no DRED present, or an opus_errorcodes value

functions.name: opus_dred_process
functions.signature: int opus_dred_process(OpusDREDDecoder *dred_dec, const OpusDRED *src, OpusDRED *dst);
functions.description: Completes CPU-intensive decoding of a DRED packet previously parsed with defer_processing=1. Often src and dst are the same state.
requirements: dred_dec must be a valid, initialized OpusDREDDecoder
src must be a valid OpusDRED state resulting from opus_dred_parse()
dst must be a valid OpusDRED state to receive updated state
Only required if opus_dred_parse() was called with defer_processing=1

functions.name: opus_decoder_dred_decode
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_dred_decode(OpusDecoder *st, const OpusDRED *dred, opus_int32 dred_offset, opus_int16 *pcm, opus_int32 frame_size);
functions.description: Decodes redundancy (DRED) audio into 16-bit PCM from a DRED state, starting at a given negative offset relative to the primary audio start.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
dred must be a valid OpusDRED containing parsed DRED data
dred_offset is the position (in samples before the start of the real audio) to decode
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (opus_int16)
frame_size must be a multiple of 2.5 ms
Returns number of decoded samples or opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_decoder_dred_decode24
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_dred_decode24(OpusDecoder *st, const OpusDRED *dred, opus_int32 dred_offset, opus_int32 *pcm, opus_int32 frame_size);
functions.description: Decodes redundancy (DRED) audio into 24-bit-depth (packed in 32-bit int) PCM from a DRED state, starting at the given offset.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
dred must be a valid OpusDRED
dred_offset is the position to decode (samples before primary audio)
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (opus_int32)
frame_size must be a multiple of 2.5 ms
Returns number of decoded samples or opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_decoder_dred_decode_float
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_dred_decode_float(OpusDecoder *st, const OpusDRED *dred, opus_int32 dred_offset, float *pcm, opus_int32 frame_size);
functions.description: Decodes redundancy (DRED) audio into float PCM from a DRED state, starting at the given offset.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
dred must be a valid OpusDRED
dred_offset is the position to decode (samples before primary audio)
pcm must have capacity for frame_size*channels samples (float)
frame_size must be a multiple of 2.5 ms
Returns number of decoded samples or opus_errorcodes

functions.name: opus_packet_parse
functions.signature: int opus_packet_parse(const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, unsigned char *out_toc, const unsigned char *frames[48], opus_int16 size[48], int *payload_offset);
functions.description: Parses an Opus packet into one or more frame pointers and sizes without copying frame data. Most applications rely on the decoder to do this internally.
requirements: data must point to a valid Opus packet
len is the size in bytes of data
out_toc may be NULL or a pointer to receive the TOC byte
frames must be able to store up to 48 frame pointers
size must be able to store up to 48 frame sizes
payload_offset if non-NULL receives the byte offset of payload within the packet
Returns number of frames

functions.name: opus_packet_get_bandwidth
functions.signature: int opus_packet_get_bandwidth(const unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Returns the audio bandwidth indicated by an Opus packet’s TOC (e.g., narrowband to fullband), or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on error.
requirements: data must point to a valid Opus packet (at least 1 byte)

functions.name: opus_packet_get_samples_per_frame
functions.signature: int opus_packet_get_samples_per_frame(const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 Fs);
functions.description: Returns the number of samples per frame as signaled by the packet’s TOC for a given sampling rate.
requirements: data must contain at least one byte
Fs must be a multiple of 400 Hz; otherwise results may be inaccurate

functions.name: opus_packet_get_nb_channels
functions.signature: int opus_packet_get_nb_channels(const unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Returns the number of channels indicated by an Opus packet, or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on error.
requirements: data must point to a valid Opus packet

functions.name: opus_packet_get_nb_frames
functions.signature: int opus_packet_get_nb_frames(const unsigned char packet[], opus_int32 len);
functions.description: Returns the number of frames contained in an Opus packet.
requirements: packet must point to a valid Opus packet
len is the byte length of packet
Returns OPUS_BAD_ARG for insufficient data, OPUS_INVALID_PACKET for corrupted/unsupported data

functions.name: opus_packet_get_nb_samples
functions.signature: int opus_packet_get_nb_samples(const unsigned char packet[], opus_int32 len, opus_int32 Fs);
functions.description: Returns the total number of samples contained in an Opus packet at the given sampling rate.
requirements: packet must point to a valid Opus packet
len is the byte length of packet
Fs must be a multiple of 400 Hz; otherwise results may be inaccurate
May return OPUS_BAD_ARG for insufficient data or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on invalid/corrupt input

functions.name: opus_packet_has_lbrr
functions.signature: int opus_packet_has_lbrr(const unsigned char packet[], opus_int32 len);
functions.description: Checks whether an Opus packet contains LBRR (in-band redundant) data. Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise, or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on error.
requirements: packet must point to a valid Opus packet
len is the byte length of packet

functions.name: opus_decoder_get_nb_samples
functions.signature: int opus_decoder_get_nb_samples(const OpusDecoder *dec, const unsigned char packet[], opus_int32 len);
functions.description: Returns the number of decoded samples (per channel) an OpusDecoder would produce from the given packet.
requirements: dec must be a valid, initialized OpusDecoder
packet must point to a valid Opus packet
len is the byte length of packet
May return OPUS_BAD_ARG for insufficient data or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on invalid/corrupt input

functions.name: opus_pcm_soft_clip
functions.signature: void opus_pcm_soft_clip(float *pcm, int frame_size, int channels, float *softclip_mem);
functions.description: Applies soft clipping to a float PCM buffer in-place to constrain samples within [-1, 1] while minimizing distortion.
requirements: pcm must point to interleaved float samples of length frame_size*channels
frame_size is the number of samples per channel to process
channels is the number of channels
softclip_mem must point to at least one float per channel and should be initialized to 0 for a new stream/state

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_get_size
functions.signature: int opus_repacketizer_get_size(void);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusRepacketizer state.

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_init
functions.signature: OpusRepacketizer *opus_repacketizer_init(OpusRepacketizer *rp);
functions.description: (Re)initializes a pre-allocated OpusRepacketizer and clears any queued frames. Call to reset when configuration changes or 120 ms total duration is reached.
requirements: rp must point to memory of at least opus_repacketizer_get_size() bytes
Must be called to reset state before changing coding mode/bandwidth/frame size/channel count or after accumulating 120 ms of audio

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_create
functions.signature: OpusRepacketizer *opus_repacketizer_create(void);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new OpusRepacketizer.

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_destroy
functions.signature: void opus_repacketizer_destroy(OpusRepacketizer *rp);
functions.description: Frees an OpusRepacketizer allocated by opus_repacketizer_create().
requirements: rp should be a pointer returned by opus_repacketizer_create()

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_cat
functions.signature: int opus_repacketizer_cat(OpusRepacketizer *rp, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len);
functions.description: Submits an Opus packet to the repacketizer queue. All packets since the last init must share mode, bandwidth, frame size, and channel count; total queued duration must not exceed 120 ms.
requirements: rp must be a valid, initialized OpusRepacketizer
data must point to packet bytes that remain valid until the next opus_repacketizer_init() or opus_repacketizer_destroy()
len is the packet size in bytes
Packets must have a valid TOC sequence compatible with those already queued
Total queued audio must not exceed 120 ms
Returns OPUS_OK on success or OPUS_INVALID_PACKET on incompatibility/invalid TOC/overflow

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_out_range
functions.signature: opus_int32 opus_repacketizer_out_range(OpusRepacketizer *rp, int begin, int end, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 maxlen);
functions.description: Constructs an output packet from a subset of frames currently queued in the repacketizer (frames [begin, end)).
requirements: rp must be a valid, initialized OpusRepacketizer with frames queued
begin and end must define a valid range: begin >= 0, begin < end, end <= opus_repacketizer_get_nb_frames(rp)
data must have capacity of at least maxlen bytes
To guarantee success: maxlen >= 1276 for a single frame, or 1277*(end-begin) for multiple frames; alternatively, 1*(end-begin) + total submitted data size since last init is sufficient
Returns total size on success; OPUS_BAD_ARG for invalid range; OPUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if maxlen insufficient

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_get_nb_frames
functions.signature: int opus_repacketizer_get_nb_frames(OpusRepacketizer *rp);
functions.description: Returns the total number of frames currently queued in the repacketizer since the last init/create.
requirements: rp must be a valid, initialized OpusRepacketizer

functions.name: opus_repacketizer_out
functions.signature: opus_int32 opus_repacketizer_out(OpusRepacketizer *rp, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 maxlen);
functions.description: Constructs a single packet containing all frames currently queued in the repacketizer.
requirements: rp must be a valid, initialized OpusRepacketizer with frames queued
data must have capacity of at least maxlen bytes
To guarantee success: maxlen >= 1277*opus_repacketizer_get_nb_frames(rp); alternatively, 1*nb_frames plus total submitted data size since last init may suffice
Returns total size on success or OPUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if maxlen insufficient

functions.name: opus_packet_pad
functions.signature: int opus_packet_pad(unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int32 new_len);
functions.description: Pads a mono/stereo Opus packet to a larger size, possibly changing the TOC sequence, without altering decoded audio.
requirements: data must point to a valid Opus packet buffer that can be overwritten in place
len must be at least 1
new_len must be >= len
Returns OPUS_OK on success, OPUS_BAD_ARG if len < 1 or new_len < len, OPUS_INVALID_PACKET if data is not a valid Opus packet

functions.name: opus_packet_unpad

functions.name: opus_multistream_packet_unpad

functions.name: opus_multistream_encoder_create
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT OpusMSEncoder *opus_multistream_encoder_create(opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int streams, int coupled_streams, const unsigned char *mapping, int application, int *error) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5);

requirements: channels must be at most 255 and may be greater than streams + coupled_streams
streams must be no more than channels
coupled_streams must be no larger than streams
streams + coupled_streams must be no more than the number of input channels
mapping must be a valid const unsigned char array of length channels describing the mapping per opus_multistream
The encoder does not allow encoding coupled streams for which one channel is unused

functions.name: opus_multistream_surround_encoder_create

mapping must be a valid const unsigned char array of length channels describing the mapping (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6))
The encoder does not allow encoding coupled streams for which one channel is unused

functions.name: opus_multistream_surround_encoder_init
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT int opus_multistream_surround_encoder_init(OpusMSEncoder *st, opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int mapping_family, int *streams, int *coupled_streams, unsigned char *mapping, int application) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(7);

requirements: st must be a valid, pre-allocated OpusMSEncoder buffer of sufficient size for the derived streams/coupled_streams
channels is the number of input channels (header does not explicitly restate upper bound; Opus commonly limits to <=255)
streams must be non-NULL (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5))
coupled_streams must be non-NULL (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6))
mapping must be non-NULL and have space for channels entries (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(7))
mapping_family selects the channel mapping family; exact accepted values are not specified in this header
application must be one of OPUS_APPLICATION_VOIP, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, or OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY

functions.name: opus_multistream_encode
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_encode(OpusMSEncoder *st, const opus_int16 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Encodes one Opus multistream frame from interleaved 16-bit PCM input into a single multistream packet. Returns the number of bytes in the encoded packet or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved input with frame_size*channels samples (non-NULL)
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder sampling rate (e.g., at 48 kHz: 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920, 2880)
data must point to a buffer with at least max_data_bytes bytes (non-NULL)
max_data_bytes specifies the available output capacity; using it solely as bitrate control is discouraged (use OPUS_SET_BITRATE)

functions.name: opus_multistream_encode24
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_encode24(OpusMSEncoder *st, const opus_int32 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Encodes one Opus multistream frame from interleaved 24-bit-style fixed-point input (stored in 32-bit integers). Returns the encoded packet length in bytes or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved input with frame_size*channels samples (non-NULL). Samples represent (or slightly exceed) 24-bit values
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder sampling rate
data must point to a buffer with at least max_data_bytes bytes (non-NULL)

functions.name: opus_multistream_encode_float
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_encode_float(OpusMSEncoder *st, const float *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Encodes one Opus multistream frame from interleaved floating-point PCM input. Returns the encoded packet length in bytes or a negative error code on failure. Typical input range is +/-1.0; values outside may be clipped by integer decoders.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSEncoder
pcm must point to interleaved input with frame_size*channels samples (non-NULL)
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder sampling rate
data must point to a buffer with at least max_data_bytes bytes (non-NULL)

functions.name: opus_multistream_encoder_destroy
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT void opus_multistream_encoder_destroy(OpusMSEncoder *st);
functions.description: Frees an OpusMSEncoder previously allocated by opus_multistream_encoder_create() or the surround create. Safe to call once per allocated encoder.
requirements: st must be a pointer previously returned by an Opus multistream encoder create function or NULL behavior is unspecified in this header

functions.name: opus_multistream_decoder_get_size

functions.description: Allocates and initializes an Opus multistream decoder with an explicit mapping. On success returns a pointer to a new OpusMSDecoder and sets *error to OPUS_OK; on failure returns NULL and sets *error to a negative code. Destroy with opus_multistream_decoder_destroy().
requirements: channels must be at most 255 and may differ from streams + coupled_streams
streams must be no more than 255

functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT int opus_multistream_decoder_init(OpusMSDecoder *st, opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int streams, int coupled_streams, const unsigned char *mapping) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6);

streams must be no more than 255

functions.name: opus_multistream_decode
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_decode(OpusMSDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int16 *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Decodes a multistream Opus packet to interleaved 16-bit PCM. If data is NULL, performs packet loss concealment (PLC). If decode_fec is 1, attempts to decode in-band FEC if available. Returns the number of samples per channel decoded or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSDecoder
data may be NULL to indicate packet loss; otherwise must point to len bytes of an Opus multistream packet
pcm must have space for frame_size*channels samples (non-NULL)
frame_size is the available samples per channel in pcm; if less than the maximum packet duration (120 ms; 5760 at 48 kHz), some packets cannot be decoded
For PLC (data == NULL) or FEC (decode_fec == 1), frame_size must be exactly the duration of the missing audio and must be a multiple of 2.5 ms
decode_fec must be 0 or 1

functions.name: opus_multistream_decode24
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_decode24(OpusMSDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, opus_int32 *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Decodes a multistream Opus packet to interleaved 24-bit-style fixed-point output (stored in 32-bit integers). Supports PLC when data is NULL and optional in-band FEC when decode_fec is 1. Returns samples per channel decoded or a negative error code.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSDecoder
data may be NULL to indicate packet loss; otherwise must point to len bytes of an Opus multistream packet
pcm must have space for frame_size*channels samples (non-NULL)

frame_size guidance identical to 16-bit decode: if less than 120 ms (5760 at 48 kHz), some packets cannot be decoded; for PLC or FEC, frame_size must equal the missing duration and be a multiple of 2.5 ms
decode_fec must be 0 or 1

functions.name: opus_multistream_decode_float
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_multistream_decode_float(OpusMSDecoder *st, const unsigned char *data, opus_int32 len, float *pcm, int frame_size, int decode_fec) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Decodes a multistream Opus packet to interleaved floating-point PCM. Supports PLC when data is NULL and optional in-band FEC. Returns samples per channel decoded or a negative error code.
requirements: st must be a valid, initialized OpusMSDecoder
data may be NULL to indicate packet loss; otherwise must point to len bytes of an Opus multistream packet
pcm must have space for frame_size*channels floats (non-NULL)
frame_size constraints as with other decoders: < 120 ms may limit decodability; for PLC or FEC, frame_size must equal the missing duration and be a multiple of 2.5 ms
decode_fec must be 0 or 1

functions.name: opus_multistream_decoder_destroy

functions.name: opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_get_size
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT opus_int32 opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_get_size(int channels, int mapping_family);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold an OpusProjectionEncoder configured for the given channel count and mapping family. Use this when allocating the encoder state with a custom allocator. Returns a negative opus error code on failure.
requirements: channels must be no more than 255.
mapping_family selects the projection mapping; valid values are library-defined; exact range not specified in this header.
On error, a negative value from opus_errorcodes is returned and must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_create
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT OpusProjectionEncoder *opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_create(opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int mapping_family, int *streams, int *coupled_streams, int application, int *error) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an Opus projection (Ambisonics) encoder. It determines and returns the number of streams and coupled streams for the chosen mapping family. On success, returns a pointer to the encoder and writes OPUS_OK to error; on failure, returns NULL and writes an opus error code.
requirements: channels must be at most 255; it may be greater than streams+coupled_streams.
mapping_family selects the projection mapping; valid values are library-defined.
streams must be a non-NULL pointer (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4)) to receive the total number of encoded streams.
coupled_streams must be a non-NULL pointer (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5)) to receive the number of coupled (stereo) streams.
application must be one of: OPUS_APPLICATION_VOIP, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, or OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY.
error must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result code.
Caller must eventually release the returned encoder with opus_projection_encoder_destroy().
On failure, check the integer pointed to by error for an opus_errorcodes value before using the returned pointer.

functions.name: opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_init
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT int opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_init(OpusProjectionEncoder *st, opus_int32 Fs, int channels, int mapping_family, int *streams, int *coupled_streams, int application) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6);
functions.description: Initializes an already-allocated OpusProjectionEncoder with the specified configuration. Intended for callers using their own allocator. Returns OPUS_OK on success or a negative error code.
requirements: st must be a non-NULL pointer (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1)) to writable memory at least the size returned by opus_projection_ambisonics_encoder_get_size().
channels must be at most 255; it may be greater than streams+coupled_streams.
streams must be a non-NULL pointer (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(5)) and the total number of streams to encode from the input; it must be no more than channels.
coupled_streams must be a non-NULL pointer (OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(6)) and the number of coupled (2-channel) streams; it must be no larger than streams.
The total number of encoded channels (streams + coupled_streams) must be no more than the number of input channels.
mapping_family selects the projection mapping; valid values are library-defined.
application must be one of: OPUS_APPLICATION_VOIP, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, or OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY.
To reset an already initialized state, use the OPUS_RESET_STATE CTL rather than re-calling init on the same memory.

functions.name: opus_projection_encode
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_projection_encode(OpusProjectionEncoder *st, const opus_int16 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Encodes one frame of interleaved 16-bit PCM using the projection encoder. Returns the number of bytes in the encoded packet, or a negative opus error code on failure.

pcm must be a non-NULL pointer to interleaved opus_int16 samples of length frame_size * encoder_channels.

Providing < 10 ms (e.g., < 480 at 48 kHz) prevents LPC or hybrid modes; this is permitted but affects quality/mode.
data must be a non-NULL pointer with capacity of at least max_data_bytes bytes to receive the encoded packet.
max_data_bytes should be set to the available capacity and may cap instantaneous bitrate; to control bitrate use OPUS_SET_BITRATE via ctl.
On error, a negative opus_errorcodes value is returned and must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: opus_projection_encode24
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_projection_encode24(OpusProjectionEncoder *st, const opus_int32 *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);

data must be a non-NULL pointer with capacity of at least max_data_bytes bytes.
max_data_bytes limits output size; use OPUS_SET_BITRATE via ctl for general bitrate control.
On error, a negative opus_errorcodes value is returned and must be handled.

functions.name: opus_projection_encode_float
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT OPUS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT int opus_projection_encode_float(OpusProjectionEncoder *st, const float *pcm, int frame_size, unsigned char *data, opus_int32 max_data_bytes) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(2) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(4);
functions.description: Encodes one frame of interleaved floating-point PCM with nominal range [-1.0, 1.0]. Returns the encoded packet size in bytes, or a negative error code.
requirements: st must be a valid non-NULL encoder state created/initialized previously.
pcm must be a non-NULL pointer to interleaved float samples of length frame_size * encoder_channels. Values beyond ±1.0 are accepted but may clip on integer decoders.
frame_size must be a valid Opus frame size for the encoder sample rate (e.g., at 48 kHz: 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920, 2880).
Providing < 10 ms of audio prevents LPC or hybrid modes; permitted but affects encoding modes.
data must be a non-NULL pointer with capacity of at least max_data_bytes bytes.
max_data_bytes limits output size; use OPUS_SET_BITRATE via ctl for general bitrate control.
On error, a negative opus_errorcodes value is returned and must be handled.

functions.name: opus_projection_encoder_destroy
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT void opus_projection_encoder_destroy(OpusProjectionEncoder *st);

functions.name: opus_projection_encoder_ctl
functions.signature: OPUS_EXPORT int opus_projection_encoder_ctl(OpusProjectionEncoder *st, int request, ... ) OPUS_ARG_NONNULL(1);
functions.description: Performs a control (CTL) operation on the projection encoder. The request and varargs are provided via convenience macros from opus_genericctls, opus_encoderctls, opus_multistream_ctls, or opus_projection_ctls. Returns OPUS_OK on success or a negative error code.

functions.name: opus_projection_decoder_get_size

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid-ish single-stream Opus packets for common modes
# It focuses on CELT-only (audio) packets at 48 kHz with 1 or 2 channels and
# builds minimally valid headers and plausible payload sizing. While fully
# spec-compliant bitstreams require the real encoder, these packets are crafted
# to be syntactically valid enough for libopus packet-parsing utilities and
# tolerant decoders to process multiple code paths without immediate rejection.
#
# Strategy
# - Create a TOC byte with coherent fields: config (mode+bandwidth+frame size),
#   stereo flag, and frame count code.
# - Produce one or multiple frames with lengths that match the framing code:
#   * Code 0: 1 frame, implicit size (payload = all bytes)
#   * Code 1: 2 frames, equal size (payload split equally)
#   * Code 2: 2 frames, different sizes (explicit size of first via 8-bit or
#             16-bit length per RFC framing; second is remainder)
#   * Code 3: Arbitrary number of frames (1..48) with VBR, with a compact table
#             of frame sizes (padding disabled). We keep it small (<=4) here.
# - Keep total packet length modest (<= ~200 bytes) to fit fuzzer buffers.
# - Ensure at least 1 byte length for APIs that require it.
#
# Note: The audio content bits are not a valid coded spectrum; decoders may
# return an error. However, packet getters and repacketizer paths benefit from
# correct framing and size fields. Some decoders will still try to decode and
# exercise error handling and FEC branches.

# Helper: encode unsigned int in Opus VBR size table coding (1 or 2 bytes).
# For simplicity we use the 1-byte form if < 252, else 2 bytes (252 + 16-bit LE).

def _opus_size_enc(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 252:
        return bytes((n,))
    else:
        # 252 followed by 16-bit little-endian value for (n-252)
        return bytes((252,)) + struct.pack('<H', n - 252)

# Build TOC byte
# Bits: [7..0] = config(0..63) | (stereo<<2) merged in config space by spec; but
# in practice: higher 6 bits hold configuration (mode/bandwidth/framesize), bit1
# is stereo flag for SILK/CELT? To keep it coherent, we use common presets from
# known encoders by selecting a canned TOC high bits and setting frame count code
# in low 2 bits.
# We emulate common CELT configurations with known top 6-bit patterns used by
# libopus (e.g., 0x18, 0x38, 0x58, 0x78 families). We keep stereo encoded via
# separate mapping in config patterns; exact mapping is not critical for parsers.

_CELT_CONFIGS = [
    0x18,  # NB 10 ms CELT
    0x19,  # NB 20 ms CELT
    0x38,  # MB 10 ms CELT
    0x39,  # MB 20 ms CELT
    0x58,  # WB 10 ms CELT
    0x59,  # WB 20 ms CELT
    0x78,  # SWB 10 ms CELT
    0x79,  # SWB 20 ms CELT
    0x98,  # FB 10 ms CELT
    0x99,  # FB 20 ms CELT
]

def _build_toc(rng: random.Random, frame_code: int) -> int:
    cfg = rng.choice(_CELT_CONFIGS)
    # Clear the lowest 2 bits (frame count code) of config if present and OR frame_code
    toc = (cfg & 0xFC) | (frame_code & 0x03)
    return toc & 0xFF

# Construct single-stream Opus packet bytes with selected framing style

def _packet_cbr_1frame(rng: random.Random, total_payload: int) -> bytes:
    # frame_code = 0 -> one frame takes all bytes after TOC
    toc = _build_toc(rng, 0)
    frame = rng.randbytes(max(0, total_payload))
    return bytes((toc,)) + frame

def _packet_cbr_2eq(rng: random.Random, total_payload: int) -> bytes:
    # frame_code = 1 -> two equal-size frames, payload must be even
    toc = _build_toc(rng, 1)
    if total_payload < 2:
        total_payload = 2
    if total_payload % 2 == 1:
        total_payload += 1
    half = total_payload // 2
    f1 = rng.randbytes(half)
    f2 = rng.randbytes(half)
    return bytes((toc,)) + f1 + f2

def _packet_cbr_2diff(rng: random.Random, total_payload: int) -> bytes:
    # frame_code = 2 -> two frames, first size explicitly stored before frames
    toc = _build_toc(rng, 2)
    # Reserve 1 or 3 bytes for size header; pick size1 so that remaining >=1
    max_payload = max(2, total_payload)
    # choose size1 in [1, max_payload-1]
    size1 = rng.randint(1, max_payload - 1)
    size_hdr = _opus_size_enc(size1)
    # ensure header fits; if header too long compared to payload, bump payload
    header_len = len(size_hdr)
    # Guarantee there is space for frames
    pay = max_payload
    if pay < header_len + 1:  # need at least one byte for frame2
        pay = header_len + 1
    frame2_len = max(1, pay - header_len - size1)
    # Adjust if negative
    if frame2_len <= 0:
        frame2_len = 1
        size1 = max(1, pay - header_len - frame2_len)
        size_hdr = _opus_size_enc(size1)
        header_len = len(size_hdr)
    f1 = rng.randbytes(size1)
    f2 = rng.randbytes(frame2_len)
    return bytes((toc,)) + size_hdr + f1 + f2

def _packet_vbr_n(rng: random.Random, nframes: int, avg_frame: int) -> bytes:
    # frame_code = 3 -> VBR with size table and optional padding (we omit padding)
    # Build size table with nframes-1 explicit sizes, last is remainder
    toc = _build_toc(rng, 3)
    nframes = max(1, min(4, nframes))
    # choose total payload size
    total_size = max(nframes, avg_frame * nframes)
    # Build sizes (nframes-1 explicit)
    sizes = []
    remaining = total_size
    for i in range(nframes - 1):
        # pick small-ish frames to keep overall size modest
        s = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(60, remaining - (nframes - 1 - i))))
        sizes.append(s)
        remaining -= s
    last_size = max(1, remaining)
    # encode frame count byte: code 3 header uses a table starting with frame count (nframes)
    # Per RFC, after TOC comes: Frame count byte (0x80 | padding_bit<<6 | vbr=1<<7?)
    # Simpler approach used by many implementations: For code 3, next byte is frame count (nframes)
    # followed by VBR size table. We'll place a simple count byte nframes.
    # To improve compatibility, we set a count byte with VBR bit = 1 and padding = 0:
    # count_byte = 0x80 | (nframes & 0x3F)
    count_byte = 0x80 | (nframes & 0x3F)
    table = bytearray()
    for s in sizes:
        table += _opus_size_enc(s)
    # frames
    frames = b"".join([
        rng.randbytes(s) for s in sizes
    ]) + rng.randbytes(last_size)
    return bytes((toc, count_byte)) + bytes(table) + frames

# Top-level generator

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a construction path
    kind = rng.choice(["1frame", "2eq", "2diff", "vbr"])
    # Total payload budget (excluding TOC and possible headers), keep small
    budget = rng.randint(10, 160)

    if kind == "1frame":
        pkt = _packet_cbr_1frame(rng, budget)
    elif kind == "2eq":
        pkt = _packet_cbr_2eq(rng, budget)
    elif kind == "2diff":
        pkt = _packet_cbr_2diff(rng, budget)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(2, 4)
        avg = rng.randint(10, 40)
        pkt = _packet_vbr_n(rng, n, avg)

    # Ensure length constraints for various stubs (some need at least 1 byte, others accept 0)
    if len(pkt) == 0:
        pkt = b"\x00"
    # Cap to 4096 bytes hard limit per instructions (we're already small)
    if len(pkt) > 4096:
        pkt = pkt[:4096]
    return pkt

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces initial bytes for an "Opus packet buffer" output parameter.
# Although the encoder overwrites the buffer, many fuzzers seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM
# with our bytes. We therefore generate sizes and byte patterns that are interesting for
# padding/unpadding paths and general buffer handling while remaining valid as arbitrary
# writable memory. We keep size <= 1500 bytes (typical MTU-ish upper bound used by stubs)
# and vary contents to exercise different code paths when encoders copy/extend buffers.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096
DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_BYTES = 400  # a mid-size default that allows many frames at moderate bitrates

def _rand_opus_like_packet(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Create a byte sequence that looks like a plausible Opus packet, though the encoder
    will overwrite it. Useful to seed repacketizer-like logic in other paths if reused.
    - TOC byte: random but with reasonable ranges for frame duration/bandwidth.
    - Payload: random with occasional runs and zero padding to trigger run-length patterns.
    """
    if target_len <= 0:
        return b""
    # Construct a semi-sane TOC: CBR/DTX bits etc. We'll just keep it random but mask
    # to common ranges so packet inspectors don't immediately reject tiny buffers.
    toc = r.randrange(0, 256)
    # Bias: set configuration bits to valid-looking patterns occasionally
    choices = [0x00, 0x18, 0x38, 0x58, 0x78, 0x98, 0xB8, 0xD8, 0xF8]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        toc = r.choice(choices) | (r.randrange(0, 8))
    payload_len = max(0, target_len - 1)
    payload = bytearray(payload_len)
    i = 0
    while i < payload_len:
        mode = r.random()
        if mode < 0.15:
            # zero run (typical padding)
            run = r.randint(1, min(32, payload_len - i))
            # already zero-initialized; just advance
            i += run
        elif mode < 0.30:
            # 0xFF run
            run = r.randint(1, min(32, payload_len - i))
            payload[i:i+run] = b"\xFF" * run
            i += run
        elif mode < 0.55:
            # small random chunk
            chunk = r.randbytes(min(32, payload_len - i))
            payload[i:i+len(chunk)] = chunk
            i += len(chunk)
        else:
            # pattern bytes
            pat = r.randrange(0, 256)
            run = r.randint(1, min(16, payload_len - i))
            payload[i:i+run] = bytes([pat]) * run
            i += run
    return bytes([toc]) + bytes(payload)

def _choose_size(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor a spectrum of sizes: tiny, small, typical, large (<=1500), and occasionally bigger but <=4096
    buckets = [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 400, 600, 900, 1200, 1500]
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        # Rare large buffer up to MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
        return r.randint(1501, min(MAX_TOTAL_SIZE, 2048))
    return buckets[int(r.random() * len(buckets))]

def _compose_buffer(r: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix strategies to seed various consumers of FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    strat = r.random()
    if size == 0:
        return b""
    if strat < 0.25:
        # All zeros (great for observing minimum writes and padding extension)
        return bytes(size)
    if strat < 0.45:
        # All 0xFF
        return b"\xFF" * size
    if strat < 0.70:
        # Pseudo Opus-like packet content
        return _rand_opus_like_packet(r, size)
    # Mixed random with structured tail padding zone
    body = bytearray(r.randbytes(size))
    # Reserve a tail likely interpreted as padding by some paths
    tail = min(48, size)
    for i in range(size - tail, size):
        body[i] = 0
    return bytes(body)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide a target capacity to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR which the stub may resize up to max_data_bytes.
    # The stub itself selects max_data_bytes in [1,1500], so our initial size influences realloc path.
    target_size = _choose_size(r)
    # Occasionally bias to DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_BYTES to match typical use
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        target_size = DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_BYTES
    buf = _compose_buffer(r, target_size)
    # Ensure final size constraint
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    return buf

from typing import List

# This generator produces plausible Opus packets that may contain a DRED payload
# region for use with opus_dred_parse(). While opus_dred_parse() in the target
# stub is fed an arbitrary byte string, providing inputs that resemble real Opus
# packet structures increases the chance of exercising meaningful parser paths.
#
# Strategy:
# - Construct a minimally valid-looking Opus packet with a plausible TOC byte.
# - Optionally include LBRR/DRED-like extension bytes after the primary frame(s),
#   including a simple header and variable-length payload with sizes that align
#   with typical Opus coding unit sizes (multiples of 2.5 ms at 48 kHz -> 120 samples
#   per frame; we reflect this via lengths but do not synthesize real audio).
# - Vary frame count (1, 2, or code 3 indicating CELT-only/TX frames), padding,
#   and include optional FEC-like marker bytes to trigger alternate code paths.
# - Keep total size under 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: This is not a full Opus encoder. It emits byte patterns that follow some
# structural conventions so that libopus packet utilities may parse portions, and
# the DRED parser may find recognizable structures.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Common TOC construction helpers
BANDWIDTH_CODES = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]  # NB, MB, WB, SWB, FB (as typical in Opus)
FRAME_SIZE_CODES = [0, 1, 2, 3]    # 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms in TOC nibble (varies with mode)
CONFIG_MODES = [0, 1, 2]           # SILK, HYBRID, CELT-like grouping across bitfields


def _rand_vlint(rng: random.Random, value: int) -> bytes:
    """Encode a small integer in a variable-length 1-2 byte style to mimic
    some internal length encodings. Not actual Opus code but plausible."""
    value = max(0, min(value, 0x3FFF))
    if value < 0x80:
        return bytes([value])
    return bytes([(0x80 | (value & 0x7F)), ((value >> 7) & 0x7F)])


def _gen_primary_frames(rng: random.Random, nb_channels: int, frame_count: int, base_bytes_per_frame: int) -> List[bytes]:
    frames = []
    for _ in range(frame_count):
        # Size heuristic: vary around base with channel multiplier
        size = base_bytes_per_frame + rng.randint(-4, 12)
        size = max(5, size) * max(1, nb_channels)
        # Fill with structured but arbitrary data
        body = bytearray(size)
        tone = rng.choice([0x00, 0x55, 0xAA, 0xFF])
        for i in range(size):
            body[i] = (tone + i * 13 + rng.randint(0, 7)) & 0xFF
        frames.append(bytes(body))
    return frames


def _maybe_pad(rng: random.Random, packet: bytearray) -> None:
    # With some probability, append Opus padding scheme: a 0x00 padding control followed by padding bytes.
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        # Use the Opus padding approach: 0x00 one or more times; but keep simple here
        pad_len = rng.randint(1, min(64, MAX_TOTAL - len(packet)))
        packet.extend(b"\x00" * pad_len)


def _gen_dred_section(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # DRED-like blob: [tag 'D'][flags][ts_offset vlint][num_samp vlint][payload][trailer]
    # Tag helps the parser find recognizable markers; not required but useful to stabilize parsing.
    if max_len <= 6:
        return b""
    flags = 0
    # Randomly set defer-processing hint bit pattern in our private layout
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        flags |= 0x01
    # Choose a small number of samples to keep overall length reasonable
    num_samp = rng.choice([120, 240, 480, 960, 1920, 2880])
    # Negative timestamp offset represented as unsigned magnitude here; parser gets offset externally
    ts_off = rng.choice([0, 120, 240, 480])

    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr.extend(b"D")
    hdr.append(flags)
    enc_ts = _rand_vlint(rng, ts_off)
    enc_ns = _rand_vlint(rng, num_samp)
    hdr.extend(enc_ts)
    hdr.extend(enc_ns)

    remain = max_len - len(hdr) - 1
    if remain <= 0:
        return b""
    # Payload bytes: patterned for compressible content
    pay_len = rng.randint(min(8, remain), min(remain, 256))
    payload = bytearray(pay_len)
    base = rng.choice([0x11, 0x2C, 0x3F, 0x80])
    for i in range(pay_len):
        payload[i] = (base + (i * (1 + (flags & 1))) + rng.randint(0, 3)) & 0xFF

    trailer = bytes([0xDF])
    return bytes(hdr) + bytes(payload) + trailer


def _build_opus_like_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose channels 1 or 2 to align with typical mono/stereo packets
    ch = 1 + (rng.randint(0, 1))
    # Build TOC: | config(5) | stereo(1) | frame count code(2) |
    cfg = (rng.choice(CONFIG_MODES) << 3) | (rng.choice(BANDWIDTH_CODES) & 0x07)
    stereo_bit = 1 if ch == 2 else 0
    count_code = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])  # one frame, two frames, arbitrary code 2 (CFR)
    toc = ((cfg & 0x1F) << 3) | ((stereo_bit & 1) << 2) | (count_code & 0x3)

    # Frame count selection
    frame_count = 1 if count_code == 0 else 2

    # Base frame size heuristic driven by frame size code
    fsc = rng.choice(FRAME_SIZE_CODES)
    base_bytes = {0: 12, 1: 20, 2: 40, 3: 80}[fsc]

    frames = _gen_primary_frames(rng, ch, frame_count, base_bytes)

    # Assemble packet
    pkt = bytearray([toc])

    # For 2 frames, include simple size byte(s) to mimic VBR list
    if frame_count == 2:
        pkt.append(len(frames[0]) & 0xFF)
        pkt.extend(frames[0])
        pkt.extend(frames[1])
    else:
        pkt.extend(frames[0])

    # Optional padding
    _maybe_pad(rng, pkt)

    # Optional LBRR/FEC-like marker followed by DRED-like section to target opus_dred_parse
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        # Marker 0xFE then a length vlint then the DRED bytes
        pkt.append(0xFE)
        # Reserve some space for DRED section
        max_dred = min(300, MAX_TOTAL - len(pkt) - 3)
        dred_blob = _gen_dred_section(rng, max_dred)
        dred_len_enc = _rand_vlint(rng, len(dred_blob))
        pkt.extend(dred_len_enc)
        pkt.extend(dred_blob)

    # Ensure final bound
    if len(pkt) > MAX_TOTAL:
        del pkt[MAX_TOTAL:]
    return bytes(pkt)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Mix seed with a small random stride to vary outputs across calls with the same base seed
    salt = rng.getrandbits(32)
    rng.seed((seed ^ 0x9E3779B1) + salt)

    # Randomly choose between: a) opus-like packet with DRED blob, b) standalone DRED blob,
    # c) short empty/near-empty payload (valid edge case: len=0 acceptable to parser as no DRED).
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.7:
        return _build_opus_like_packet(rng)
    elif choice < 0.9:
        # Standalone DRED-like blob
        length = rng.randint(16, 256)
        return _gen_dred_section(rng, length)
    else:
        # Edge case: empty or minimal
        return b"" if rng.random() < 0.5 else bytes([0xFE, 0x00])

import random
from typing import List

# Opus packet basics we will craft:
# - 1-byte TOC (Table of Contents): bits encode config, bandwidth, frame size, stereo flag, and frame count code (F)
# - Followed by frame data and optional padding. For the purposes of pad/unpad APIs,
#   they mostly validate structure and TOC/F bits; they do not require decodable audio bits,
#   but a structurally well-formed packet helps exercise more code paths.
#
# We will generate a range of valid packet layouts:
# - Code 0: 1 frame
# - Code 1: 2 equal-size frames
# - Code 2: 2 frames, sizes given explicitly (VBR)
# - Code 3: Arbitrary number of frames (1..48) in a self-delimiting framing (CELT-only)
# For simplicity and good validity coverage without full CELT/SILK frames, we craft consistent
# lengths and plausible size bytes. The frame payload bytes themselves are arbitrary; only sizes
# and count must match the declared structure so that parsers accept the packet.
# We will also occasionally add RFC6716-style padding extension so unpad can strip, and pad can add.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

BW_VALUES = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]  # NB, MB, WB, SWB, FB encodings in TOC
FRAME_SIZE_CODES = [0, 1, 2, 3]  # 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms etc.; exact mapping not needed for structure


def _build_toc(stereo: bool, fcode: int) -> int:
    # TOC layout (simplified):
    #  bits 7..5: config (mode/bandwidth) – we choose a plausible combination
    #  bits 4..3: frame size code
    #  bit 2: stereo flag (0 mono, 1 stereo) – only meaningful for CELT, but safe
    #  bits 1..0: code (F) frame count code 0..3
    # We pick config by mixing a generic mode + bandwidth. Using lower values is commonly accepted.
    config = (random.choice(BW_VALUES) & 0x07)  # keep 3 bits
    fs = (random.choice(FRAME_SIZE_CODES) & 0x03)
    s = 1 if stereo else 0
    toc = (config << 5) | (fs << 3) | (s << 2) | (fcode & 0x03)
    return toc


def _leb128_like(n: int) -> List[int]:
    # Opus code 3 uses self-delimiting frames where lengths are encoded in 1 or 2 bytes
    # with 0xFF continuation. We'll emit a simple scheme using 0xFF chunks then remainder.
    out = []
    while n >= 255:
        out.append(255)
        n -= 255
    out.append(n)
    return out


def _add_padding(buf: bytearray, pad_len: int) -> None:
    # RFC6716 padding extension: add a padding byte 0x00 followed by padding bytes.
    # Opus padding uses a sequence of 0x00 and length bytes 0xFF to accumulate size.
    # For simplicity, we append: 0x00, then chunks of 0xFF summing to pad_len-1, finally remainder.
    if pad_len <= 0:
        return
    pad_len_remaining = pad_len
    # First extension byte 0x00 signals padding present and starts the pad count accumulation.
    buf.append(0)
    pad_len_remaining -= 1
    while pad_len_remaining >= 255:
        buf.append(255)
        pad_len_remaining -= 255
    if pad_len_remaining > 0:
        buf.append(pad_len_remaining)


def _packet_code0_or1(stereo: bool, two_equal: bool) -> bytes:
    # Code 0: single frame, Code 1: 2 equal-size frames.
    fcode = 1 if two_equal else 0
    toc = _build_toc(stereo, fcode)
    # Choose a small frame size to keep total under limit.
    frame_bytes = random.randint(10, 80)
    if two_equal:
        payload = bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(frame_bytes * 2))
    else:
        payload = bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(frame_bytes))
    pkt = bytearray([toc])
    pkt.extend(payload)
    # Optional padding 0..64
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        _add_padding(pkt, random.randint(1, 64))
    return bytes(pkt)


def _packet_code2_vbr(stereo: bool) -> bytes:
    # Code 2: 2 frames with explicit lengths (VBR). Format: TOC, size1, frame1, frame2
    toc = _build_toc(stereo, 2)
    # Choose two frames with variable sizes
    f1 = random.randint(5, 60)
    f2 = random.randint(5, 90)
    # For sizes, if >= 252, would require 2 bytes in real spec, but we keep small to use 1 byte.
    size_bytes = bytes([f1])
    payload = bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(f1 + f2))
    pkt = bytearray([toc])
    pkt.extend(size_bytes)
    pkt.extend(payload)
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        _add_padding(pkt, random.randint(1, 64))
    return bytes(pkt)


def _packet_code3_multiframe(stereo: bool) -> bytes:
    # Code 3: N (1..48) self-delimited frames. Layout:
    # TOC, byte: ch (N-1 in lower 6 bits) and padding flag; then for all frames except last, length codes; then frames
    # We'll create a moderate N (2..6) to keep small and valid.
    n = random.randint(2, 6)
    toc = _build_toc(stereo, 3)
    pkt = bytearray([toc])
    # Indicate VBR (self-delimited) and no padding flag in this length header byte is not explicit in spec here;
    # For broad acceptance, we set the high bit to 0 (no padding), and encode (n-1) in lower 6 bits, and set VBR flag.
    # In Opus code 3, second byte: M (VBR flag bit 7), padding flag bit 6, and count-1 in lower 6.
    vbr_flag = 0x80
    pad_flag = 0x00
    ch = (n - 1) & 0x3F
    pkt.append(vbr_flag | pad_flag | ch)
    # Choose lengths and write them as self-delimiting (all but last frame)
    lengths = [random.randint(8, 64) for _ in range(n)]
    for L in lengths[:-1]:
        pkt.extend(_leb128_like(L))
    # Append payload frames
    for L in lengths:
        pkt.extend(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(L))
    # Optional additional padding section via pad flag pathway is complex; instead, append extension style
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        _add_padding(pkt, random.randint(1, 64))
    return bytes(pkt)


def _generate_valid_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Use supplied rng by seeding python's random module for simplicity
    random.setstate(rng.getstate())
    stereo = rng.choice([False, True])
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.3:
        pkt = _packet_code0_or1(stereo, two_equal=False)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        pkt = _packet_code0_or1(stereo, two_equal=True)
    elif choice < 0.85:
        pkt = _packet_code2_vbr(stereo)
    else:
        pkt = _packet_code3_multiframe(stereo)
    # Ensure at least 1 byte and not exceeding MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
    if len(pkt) < 1:
        pkt = bytes([_build_toc(stereo, 0)])
    return pkt[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pkt = _generate_valid_packet(rng)
    # Fuzzer stubs expect a mutable std::string buffer with size>=1. We return bytes; harness will write it.
    # Keep size reasonable and non-empty.
    if len(pkt) < 1:
        pkt = b"\x00"
    return pkt

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# Generator for a demixing matrix blob used by opus_projection_decoder_{create,init} fuzzers.
# Although the fuzzer accepts arbitrary bytes, we bias towards shapes that look
# like plausible demixing matrices so the target reaches deeper code paths.
# We construct a header with dimensions and a payload of coefficients in various
# encodings (float32, Q8.8, S7.8 dB-like, sparse patterns), then optionally
# compress or pad. Max total size limited to 1024 bytes per stub; we cap <= 1024.

MAX_SIZE = 1024


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _make_dims(rng):
    # Opus projection decoders use: output channels (C), coded streams (S), coupled streams (Sc).
    # Choose small to moderate values to fit into size budget, but vary for coverage.
    C = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 16])
    # Total coded channels = S + Sc, with Sc <= S typically. Keep small.
    S = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8])
    Sc = rng.randrange(0, min(S, 4) + 1)
    return C, S, Sc


def _gen_coeff_float32(rng, count):
    # Generate float32 coefficients in a few interesting ranges
    out = bytearray()
    modes = [
        lambda: rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0),            # normalized gains
        lambda: rng.uniform(-8.0, 8.0),            # wider
        lambda: 0.0,                               # zeros
        lambda: 1.0,                               # ones
        lambda: rng.choice([-0.5, 0.5, -1.0, 1.0]) # typical boundaries
    ]
    # Pick a dominant mode with occasional spikes
    dominant = rng.choice(modes)
    for i in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.05:
            val = _rand_choice(rng, [0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 2.0, -2.0, 0.7071, -0.7071])
        else:
            val = dominant()
        out += struct.pack('<f', float(val))
    return bytes(out)


def _gen_coeff_q8_8(rng, count):
    # Fixed-point Q8.8 ints
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        # values around 0..256 range in Q8.8
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            q = _rand_choice(rng, [0, 256, -256, 128, -128])
        else:
            q = int(rng.uniform(-512, 512))
        out += struct.pack('<h', q)
    return bytes(out)


def _gen_sparse_matrix(C, cols, rng, coeff_bytes_fn):
    # Row-major: for each output channel, mostly zeros with a few non-zeros
    total = C * cols
    # Prepare baseline zeros as 4-byte or 2-byte depending on generator
    sample = coeff_bytes_fn(rng, 1)
    elem_size = len(sample)
    buf = bytearray(sample * total)
    # Make some non-zero entries
    non_zero_per_row = max(1, min(cols, rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3])))
    for r in range(C):
        nz_idx = rng.sample(range(cols), non_zero_per_row)
        for c in nz_idx:
            pos = (r * cols + c) * elem_size
            buf[pos:pos+elem_size] = coeff_bytes_fn(rng, 1)
    return bytes(buf)


def _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag, elem_size, rows, cols):
    # Simple ad-hoc header to look structured: magic, version, dims, fmt, sizes
    magic = b'OPDM'  # Opus Projection DeMix
    version = rng.choice([1, 2])
    # header: magic(4) ver(1) C(1) S(1) Sc(1) fmt(1) elem(1) rows(1) cols(1) rsv(2)
    return struct.pack('<4sBBBBBBBBH', magic, version, C & 0xFF, S & 0xFF, Sc & 0xFF,
                       fmt_tag & 0xFF, elem_size & 0xFF, rows & 0xFF, cols & 0xFF, 0)


def _maybe_wrap(rng, payload):
    # Occasionally prepend a tiny TLV-ish wrapper or checksum to mimic containerization
    choice = rng.random()
    out = bytearray()
    if choice < 0.25:
        # TLV: type=1 length=payload
        out += struct.pack('<BI', 1, len(payload))
        out += payload
    elif choice < 0.50:
        # Add CRC32 then payload
        crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        out += struct.pack('<I', crc)
        out += payload
    else:
        out += payload
    return bytes(out)


def _maybe_pad(rng, data, max_size):
    # Pad or truncate to fit limits; padding with zeros or pattern
    if len(data) > max_size:
        return data[:max_size]
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_len = rng.randrange(0, max_size - len(data) + 1)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pad = b'\x00' * pad_len
        else:
            pad = bytes([_rand_choice(rng, [0x00, 0xFF, 0x7F, 0x80]) for _ in range(pad_len)])
        return data + pad
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy
    strategy = rng.choice([
        'float_dense',
        'float_sparse',
        'q88_dense',
        'q88_sparse',
        'mixed_blocks',
    ])

    C, S, Sc = _make_dims(rng)

    # Columns represent coded channels; choose either S or S+Sc to vary
    cols_mode = rng.choice(['streams', 'coded'])
    cols = S if cols_mode == 'streams' else min(16, S + Sc)
    rows = C

    chunks = []

    if strategy == 'float_dense':
        coeff = _gen_coeff_float32(rng, rows * cols)
        header = _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag=1, elem_size=4, rows=rows, cols=cols)
        chunks.append(header + coeff)

    elif strategy == 'float_sparse':
        coeff = _gen_sparse_matrix(C, cols, rng, lambda r, n: _gen_coeff_float32(r, n))
        header = _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag=2, elem_size=4, rows=rows, cols=cols)
        chunks.append(header + coeff)

    elif strategy == 'q88_dense':
        coeff = _gen_coeff_q8_8(rng, rows * cols)
        header = _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag=3, elem_size=2, rows=rows, cols=cols)
        chunks.append(header + coeff)

    elif strategy == 'q88_sparse':
        coeff = _gen_sparse_matrix(C, cols, rng, lambda r, n: _gen_coeff_q8_8(r, n))
        header = _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag=4, elem_size=2, rows=rows, cols=cols)
        chunks.append(header + coeff)

    elif strategy == 'mixed_blocks':
        # Compose multiple small blocks with different formats
        num_blocks = rng.choice([2, 3, 4])
        for b in range(num_blocks):
            b_rows = rng.choice([rows, max(1, rows // 2), min(16, rows + 1)])
            b_cols = rng.choice([cols, max(1, cols // 2), min(16, cols + 1)])
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                coeff = _gen_coeff_float32(rng, b_rows * b_cols)
                tag, esz = 10, 4
            else:
                coeff = _gen_coeff_q8_8(rng, b_rows * b_cols)
                tag, esz = 11, 2
            header = _build_header(rng, C, S, Sc, fmt_tag=tag, elem_size=esz, rows=b_rows, cols=b_cols)
            chunks.append(header + coeff)

    payload = b''.join(chunks)
    payload = _maybe_wrap(rng, payload)
    payload = _maybe_pad(rng, payload, MAX_SIZE)

    # Ensure non-empty to pass non-NULL matrix paths, but still allow very small matrices.
    if len(payload) == 0:
        payload = b'\x00'

    # Final safety cap (fuzzer resizes to <=1024 as well)
    return payload[:MAX_SIZE]
